Balance.description: One balance: how far it is from closing, and what that is measured against.

imbalance.description: The imbalance as a share of the reference.

oneOf.description: The imbalance is within the tolerance.
The imbalance is over the tolerance, or there is nothing to compare it with.
There is nothing to balance, as in a closed domain. Never a pass.

BlobKind.description: What kind of result a stored blob is.

oneOf.description: Prepared geometry.
A generated mesh.
A solver result.

BlobRef.description: A result kept in the content-addressed store beside the file.

size.description: Size of the content in bytes.

BoundaryCondition.description: One named boundary: the box faces it covers, its kind, and a speed where the kind needs one.

velocity.description: Required for a velocity inlet and a moving wall; absent for every other kind.

BoundaryKind.description: What a boundary does to the flow.

oneOf.description: Fixed inflow velocity. `velocity` is the speed into the domain, along the inward normal.
Outflow at gauge pressure zero in kinematic units. It has no value field.
Wall with zero velocity at the wall.
Wall without friction.

Wall that moves in its own plane. `velocity` is the tangential speed along +x (bottom
and top faces) or +y (left and right faces).
Mirror plane.

Check.description: One named check a run was held to.

detail.description: A short statement of what was found.

Checkpoint.description: The latest written time of a stopped run, kept so a later run can start from it.

blob.description: The hash of the stored blob.

size.description: The size of the stored blob in bytes.

time.description: The solver time written, as plain decimal text.

compared.description: How many names were compared: the union of both sides.

differing.description: Every quantity that is not identical (including those within tolerance), sorted by name.

max_abs_diff.description: The largest difference over the names present on both sides, 0 when there are none.

ContentHash.description: BLAKE3 hash of a stored result, as 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

ContinuedFrom.description: The run a continued run took its starting state from.

run.description: The id of the earlier run.

time.description: The solver time it started from, as plain decimal text.

open.description:
True when the box has open (inlet or outlet) faces. A closed domain has only walls.
Closed unless stated.

Face.description:
A face of the box domain: left (x min), right (x max), bottom (y min) or top (y max).
The front and back faces are always empty (two-dimensional case).

GeometryRecipe.description: The size and openness of the domain, in metres.

LineMonitor.description: A straight line of evenly spaced samples; `samples` counts the points, ends included.

LineRecipe.description: A sampled line the case writes, ends in metres.

Link.description: A file the study refers to but does not contain: where it was, and what it held.

hash.description: BLAKE3 hash of the file content as recorded when the link was made.

id.description: Name the study uses for this link: 1 to 40 lower-case letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.

name.description: File name as recorded when the link was made.

path.description: Path of the file, relative to the folder of the study file.

patches.description: Sorted by their JSON text, so the order never depends on boundary labels.

raw.description:
The raw overrides that touch a mesh dictionary, without their labels, sorted by file,
entry, value and backend. Absent when there are none, so a study without them keeps its
mesh key.

MonitorField.description: The field a probe or line reads.

Monitors.description:
What to watch while the solver runs. Every monitor is keyed by the user's own label; the
label is shown to people and never written into a case (the case names monitors by their
position). Labels match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}`. A study that lists no probe, line or
surface is watched at five default velocity points.

settle.description:
How steady a monitored quantity must be to count as settled. It judges a run and does not
change what is run.

surfaces.description: Integrals over a named boundary, at most 8.

MonitorsRecipe.description:
What the case watches: the centreline sample count and the planned monitors in plan order,
the default probes included, with no label and no settle tolerance. A list that is empty is
left out of the text.

Origin.description: Which sweep made a variant, and which point of it.

oneOf.description: The run went to its end.
The run was stopped on request at this solver time.

Output.description: One stage output a run recorded: its key, the recipe the key comes from, and the stored blob.

blob.description: The hash of the stored blob.

size.description: The size of the stored blob in bytes.

Output2.description: One stage output a run recorded: its key, the recipe the key comes from, and the stored blob.

blob.description: The hash of the stored blob.

size.description: The size of the stored blob in bytes.

Override.description:
One change to a study: put a value at a setting, or take a member away.

A setting is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the study written as JSON, for example
`/mesh/cells_x`. Only object members are addressed; no list element ever is, so a list such as
the faces of a boundary is replaced whole.

oneOf.description: Replace the member at `setting`, or add it when its parent exists and it does not.
Delete the member at `setting`.

PatchRecipe.description: The patch layout of one boundary: what it is and where, never what the user called it.

Probe.description: A point in the plane of the case (the case is flat, so a point has x and y only).

ProbeRecipe.description: A probe the case writes: where it reads and what, never what the user called it.

Provenance.description: What a run stood on, so it can be repeated without anything else.

geometry_hash.description: The hash of the geometry recipe.

host.description: A label for the machine it ran on; sharing may clear it.

mesh_hash.description: The hash of the mesh blob the run stands on.

mesh_key.description: The key of the mesh the run stands on.

result_key.description: The key of the result the run recorded, if it recorded one.

settings.description: The authored study as it was when the case ran.

tool.description: The tools that made the outputs.

QuantityDiff.description: One quantity that is not identical on both sides. A side that lacks the name is `None`.

abs_diff.description: `None` when a side is missing or a value is not finite.

QuantityState.description:
The numbers for one monitored quantity. They are always given, settled or not.

`samples` is the number of samples the statistics were taken over (the tail); where no tail
could be taken (an error) it is the length of the series.

RawBackend.description:
The backend a raw override is written for. The dictionary syntax differs between backends, so
an override only runs on the backend it names.

RawOverride.description: One dictionary entry to set in the written case.

backend.description: The backend this override is written for.

entry.description:
The entry inside the file: block names then the entry, joined by `/`, for example
`relaxationFactors/equations/U`.

value.description: The text that goes after the entry name.

ResultRecipe.description: What made a result: the mesh by key, and everything the solver was given.

boundaries.description: By the user's label, so a rename changes this recipe and never the mesh recipe.

raw.description:
Every raw override by the user's label, so a rename changes this recipe and never the
mesh recipe. Absent when there are none, so a study without them keeps its result key.

RunRecord.description: One run. A record is never edited after it is appended to the log.

checkpoint.description: For a stopped run, the latest written time.

checks.description: The checks the run was held to.

comparison.description: For a rerun, how it compares with the run it repeats.

continued_from.description: For a continued run, the run and time it started from.

id.description: `run-<n>`, counted from the number of records before it.

key_numbers.description: The numbers a rerun is compared on.

mesh.description: The mesh this run recorded; absent when it did not record one.

np.description: The number of processes the run used.

outcome.description: How the run ended; absent means it went to its end.

rerun_of.description: The run this one repeats, if it is a rerun.

result.description: The result this run recorded; absent when it did not record one.

scenario.description: The scenario this run was made for; absent means the study itself.

verdict.description: The convergence verdict made when the run was recorded.

Scenario.description:
A variant of a study: what it changes, and the label a person gave it.

It stores only its own overrides. Its effective study is the study it descends from with the
overrides of every ancestor applied first and its own after.

SettleSettings.description:
Optional tolerances for judging a monitored quantity settled. A member left out uses the
built-in value.

drift_rel.description: The largest drift across the tail, relative to its mean (above 0, up to 1).

spread_rel.description: The largest spread of the tail, relative to its mean (above 0, up to 1).

tail_floor.description: The fewest iterations the judged tail may hold (5 to 100000).

tail_fraction.description: The share of the iterations, counted from the end, that is judged (above 0, up to 1).

end_time.description: Steady SIMPLE iteration count, represented as solver pseudo-time in seconds.

StageKey.description: The key of one stage output: 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

oneOf.description: Flat within both tolerances over the tail.
The fitted line still moves across the tail.
Flat on average but the values spread more than the tolerance.
Fewer iteration samples than the tail floor.
Fewer write-time samples than a line monitor needs.
A non-finite value, unequal lengths or times that do not increase.

boundary_conditions.description:
Boundaries keyed by the user's own label. The label appears in diagnostics only and
never in the written case. Labels match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}`.

raw_overrides.description:
Raw dictionary overrides keyed by a label (same naming rule as boundaries). For expert
use: each one sets a solver dictionary entry the study does not model. They show in
diffs and are part of the result's identity.

SurfaceMonitor.description: A quantity integrated over one boundary of the study, named by its label.

SurfaceQuantity.description: What a surface monitor reports over its boundary.

oneOf.description: The volumetric flux through the boundary.
The area-averaged pressure on the boundary.
The area-integrated pressure on the boundary.

SurfaceRecipe.description:
A surface integral the case writes. It names the kind of boundary, as the mesh does, so two
boundaries of one kind with different names give the same entry.

Sweep.description: A sweep: the scenario it starts from and the parameters it varies.

Target.description: What a parameter changes in the study.

oneOf.description: A quantity, written in a study as `{"value": <number>, "unit": <text>}`.
A whole number, such as a cell count.
A plain number, such as a convergence limit.

A vector setting turned by an angle. The values are angles in degrees, counter-clockwise
about +z; the base vector is the one at angle zero. The two components are set as
quantities in `unit`.

Tolerance.description: How far two numbers may differ and still count as the same: an absolute part plus a part relative to their size.

ToolIdentity.description: Everything about the tools that can change an output without the study changing.

dialect.description: The solver dialect the case is written in, for example `esi-v2512`.

image_digest.description: The part of the image reference after `@`, for example `sha256:...`.

sidecar_lock.description:
The hash of the geometry sidecar's lock, or `null` when no sidecar was used. An absent
lock is written as `null`, never skipped, so absent and present keys differ.

writer_version.description: The version of this program that wrote the case.

Values.description: The values of one parameter: a list, a range or a number of even steps.

oneOf.description: The values in the order given.
From `start` by `step`; `stop` is included when the steps land on it.
`count` values spread evenly from `start` to `stop`, both included.

Verdict2.description:
The verdict with everything it was made from.

`reasons` are stable words: `no_monitored_quantity`, `not_settled:<name>`, `mass_imbalance`,
`energy_imbalance`, `residuals_above_limit`, and the two a caller adds with
[`Verdict::blocked_by`]: [`SOLVER_FAILED`] and [`NOT_FINISHED`].

description: Everything the file refers to outside itself.

pruned.description:
Hashes of stored results that were removed on purpose, sorted, each listed in `blobs`. The
run records that named them stay. Absent when nothing was removed.

runs.description: The runs recorded for this study, oldest first; the list only grows.

scenarios.description:
Variants of the study, each storing only its overrides; a variant is listed after its
parent. Absent when the study has none.

sweeps.description:
Parameter sweeps, and through each point's origin the variants they generated. Absent when
the study has none.
